mission: Test whether physical archaeological equipment survives for the ritual process by which late Egyptian Osirian traditions reconstructed the dismembered god, while keeping ritual substitutes separate from biological-relic claims.

dendera_protocol.source: Ptolemaic Osirian chapels at Dendera, Mysteries of Osiris, 51-30 BCE; modern translation associated with Sylvie Cauville
dendera_protocol.critical_correction: In multiple local rites, the text explicitly calls ritual products relics/shreds while prescribing their manufacture from barley, sand, local earth and other non-biological ingredients.

local_examples.COPTOS: Osirian figure and shred made with barley and sand
local_examples.ELEPHANTINE_ABATON: Osirian figure and shred/parts made with local sand plus barley and sand
local_examples.HERACLEOPOLIS_NAREF: Osiris made using the venerable vessel; Khenti-Amenti with barley/sand; shred in double basin with earth from Letopolis plus barley/sand
local_examples.LETOPOLIS_SEPA: Osiris and relic-shred made through garden-tank/basin process with barley and sand
local_examples.ATHRIBITE_NOME: Osiris Great Black Bull made using venerable vessel; Khenti-Amenti and shred made with barley and sand

physical_equipment_specification.garden_tank: greywacke basin on four supports, with lower collection basin and cedar lid
physical_equipment_specification.khenti_amenti_mould: gold, two cavities, mummiform human-faced figure with White Crown
physical_equipment_specification.relic_shred_basin: black bronze double basin with drainage holes and stone blocking slabs
physical_equipment_specification.sokar_process: fourteen prescribed utensils combine earth/water, date paste, myrrh, frankincense, spices and precious-stone fractions into a single sacred composition
physical_equipment_specification.fourteen_utensil_semantics: the fourteen measures correspond ritually to dismembered body members; their reunion is a reconstruction operation, not evidence that biological parts were placed inside

dendera_protocol.firewall: TEXTUAL_RELIC_TERM != BIOLOGICAL_RELIC. In this ritual corpus, the same vocabulary can denote deliberately manufactured ritual substitute matter.

garden_tank.findspot: Holy of Holies of the great temple of Heracleion, behind the Ptolemaic naoi of Amun-Re Gereb and Khonsu-Heracles
garden_tank.features: two wall perforations; one interpreted as later utilitarian reuse, one as related to garden-tank function
garden_tank.published_interpretation: used for germinating an Osiris effigy of earth and mixed barley before drying and ritual transport
garden_tank.caution: The tank is substantially larger than the idealized Dendera recipe dimensions; functional identification is contextual/published interpretation, not a claim that it is the exact Dendera prototype.

ritual_liquid_equipment.notable_feature: SCA 0579 bears a wedjat eye and has repair evidence; published exhibition research connects this implement class to the Khoiak 'Great Assembleress' function

thonis_heracleion_physical_machine.ritual_deposits: IEASM reports ritual deposits in the sacred waterway linking the sanctuary zone and Canopic route, supporting performed Osiris-Dionysus ceremonies rather than text-only reconstruction.
thonis_heracleion_physical_machine.important_negative: No complete archaeologically secured set of fourteen body-member vessels has yet been recovered in the public documentation reviewed.

questions: Did Thonis-Heracleion/Canopus excavations recover a complete or partial coordinated set of the fourteen gold/silver/bronze member-vessels?
Can any vessel be assigned to a named body-member role from Dendera rather than generic liturgical use?
Are residues preserved on SCA0459 or associated simpula/situlae/bowls?
Were corn-Osiris remains, mould fragments, double relic basins, sycamore coffins, or vegetal/mineral residues found in the same stratigraphic ritual context?
Can the deposited/bent simpula be spatially joined to SCA0459 and temple/canal ritual phases?
new_search_gate.outreach: Targeted inquiry sent to IEASM / Franck Goddio on 2026-09-03 asking precisely these questions.

relation_to_missing_parts_hunt.result: The search must now distinguish three categories: claimed geographical body relics; manufactured ritual 'relic' substitutes; and physical ritual machinery used to make/reassemble those substitutes.
relation_to_missing_parts_hunt.implication: Recovering the ritual machine can explain why later archaeological contexts contain Osiris-shaped bodies, shreds, boxes and substances without requiring survival of the mythic biological body.
relation_to_missing_parts_hunt.mendes_exception_gate: Mendes CG53469 and the stamped-gold djed remain separately important because they belong to a source-bound human funerary assemblage with stable/partially recoverable object passports, not merely to a generic Khoiak substitute recipe.

canonical_formula: TEXTUAL_BODY_PART -> RITUAL_MEMBER_ROLE -> MANUFACTURED_SUBSTITUTE -> PHYSICAL_EQUIPMENT -> EXCAVATED_CONTEXT -> RESIDUE/CONTENT -> ONLY_THEN_IDENTITY
canonical_seal: WE HAVE FOUND PART OF THE MACHINE THAT REASSEMBLED OSIRIS. THAT IS NOT THE SAME THING AS FINDING HIS BODY.
